Equilibrium of a Particle

Equilibrium of a Particle

Statics
ENGI 10115 problems
We’ll work through these together in class.
Problem 1
Ch. 3 · Q1 — Two-cable support, one horizontal cable
A $60\ \mathrm{kg}$ crate hangs from ring $A$. The ring is held by a horizontal cable $AD$ fastened to a wall on the left and by cable $AB$, which rises to the right at $35^{\circ}$ above the horizontal to a ceiling anchor $B$. Treat ring $A$ as a particle and take $g=9.81\ \mathrm{m/s^2}$.
Crate supported at ring A by cables AB and AD
Determine the tension in cable $AB$.
Solution
1030 N
Free-body diagram
Free-body diagram of ring A
Step 1Draw the free-body diagram: isolate ring $A$ from the wall, ceiling and crate. Three forces act on it: $T_{AB}$ pulling up and to the right along cable $AB$ at $35^{\circ}$, $T_{AD}$ pulling horizontally to the left along cable $AD$, and the crate weight $W$ pulling straight down.
Step 2List knowns and unknowns: known $m=60\ \mathrm{kg}$, $g=9.81\ \mathrm{m/s^2}$, angle $35^{\circ}$; unknown $T_{AB}$ (and $T_{AD}$).
Step 3State the model: ring $A$ is a particle in equilibrium under a coplanar force system; cables carry tension only, acting along the cable.
Step 4Set axes: $+x$ to the right and $+y$ upward.
Step 5Compute the weight: $$W=mg=60\ \mathrm{kg}\cdot9.81\ \mathrm{m/s^2}=588.6\ \mathrm{N}$$
Step 6Resolve $T_{AB}$ into components: $T_{AB,x}=T_{AB}\cos35^{\circ}$ (to the right) and $T_{AB,y}=T_{AB}\sin35^{\circ}$ (upward).
Step 7Sum forces in x: $$\rightarrow^{+}\ \sum F_x=T_{AB}\cos35^{\circ}-T_{AD}=0$$ This equation has two unknowns, so set it aside.
Step 8Sum forces in y: $$\uparrow^{+}\ \sum F_y=T_{AB}\sin35^{\circ}-W=0$$ Only $T_{AB}$ is unknown here because $T_{AD}$ has no vertical component.
Step 9Check moments: every force on the free body passes through point $A$, so each moment arm is zero and $\sum M_{A}=0$ is satisfied automatically; it gives no new equation, which is why a particle has only force equations.
Step 10Rearrange the y-equation: $$T_{AB}=\frac{W}{\sin35^{\circ}}$$
Step 11Substitute numbers: $$T_{AB}=\frac{588.6\ \mathrm{N}}{0.5736}=1026\ \mathrm{N}$$
Step 12State the result: $T_{AB}\approx1030\ \mathrm{N}$, a tension acting along the cable from $A$ toward $B$.
Step 13Check reasonableness: the x-equation gives $T_{AD}=1026\cos35^{\circ}=841\ \mathrm{N}>0$, so both cables pull as assumed. $T_{AB}$ exceeds the weight because only its vertical component carries the crate. Units: $\mathrm{kg\cdot m/s^2=N}$.
Worked Solution
Free-body diagram of ring A
**Given:** $m=60\ \mathrm{kg}$, $g=9.81\ \mathrm{m/s^2}$, cable $AB$ at $35^{\circ}$ above the horizontal, cable $AD$ horizontal. **Find:** $T_{AB}$. **FBD at $A$:** $T_{AB}$ (up-right at $35^{\circ}$), $T_{AD}$ (left), $W$ (down). Weight: $W=mg=60(9.81)=588.6\ \mathrm{N}$. Equilibrium with $+x$ right, $+y$ up: $$\rightarrow^{+}\ \sum F_x=T_{AB}\cos35^{\circ}-T_{AD}=0$$ $$\uparrow^{+}\ \sum F_y=T_{AB}\sin35^{\circ}-588.6\ \mathrm{N}=0$$ From the second equation, $$T_{AB}=\frac{588.6\ \mathrm{N}}{\sin35^{\circ}}=1026\ \mathrm{N}\approx1030\ \mathrm{N}.$$ Check with the first equation: $T_{AD}=1026\cos35^{\circ}=841\ \mathrm{N}$ (positive, so the cable is in tension as assumed).
Problem 2
Ch. 3 · Q2 — Two inclined ropes with a 3-4-5 slope
A $75\ \mathrm{kg}$ box hangs from knot $A$. Rope $AB$ rises to the left at $30^{\circ}$ above the horizontal. Rope $AC$ rises to the right with a slope of 3 vertical to 4 horizontal (a 3-4-5 triangle). Take $g=9.81\ \mathrm{m/s^2}$.
Box suspended from knot A by ropes AB and AC
Determine the force in rope $AC$.
Solution
693 N
Free-body diagram
Free-body diagram of knot A
Step 1Draw the free-body diagram: isolate knot $A$. Three forces act: $F_B$ along rope $AB$ (up-left at $30^{\circ}$), $F_C$ along rope $AC$ (up-right on the 3-4-5 slope), and the box weight $W$ straight down.
Step 2List knowns and unknowns: known $m=75\ \mathrm{kg}$, $g=9.81\ \mathrm{m/s^2}$, $30^{\circ}$, slope 3-4-5; unknown $F_B$ and $F_C$. Two unknowns, two equations: solvable.
Step 3State the model: knot $A$ is a particle in 2-D equilibrium; ropes carry tension only.
Step 4Set axes: $+x$ to the right and $+y$ upward.
Step 5Compute the weight: $$W=75\ \mathrm{kg}\cdot9.81\ \mathrm{m/s^2}=735.75\ \mathrm{N}$$
Step 6Resolve $F_B$ into components: $F_{B,x}=-F_B\cos30^{\circ}$ (to the left) and $F_{B,y}=F_B\sin30^{\circ}$ (upward).
Step 7Resolve $F_C$ into components: from the slope triangle, $F_{C,x}=\tfrac45F_C$ (to the right) and $F_{C,y}=\tfrac35F_C$ (upward).
Step 8Sum forces in x: $$\rightarrow^{+}\ \sum F_x=-F_B\cos30^{\circ}+\tfrac45F_C=0$$
Step 9Sum forces in y: $$\uparrow^{+}\ \sum F_y=F_B\sin30^{\circ}+\tfrac35F_C-W=0$$
Step 10Check moments: every force on the free body passes through point $A$, so each moment arm is zero and $\sum M_{A}=0$ is satisfied automatically; it gives no new equation, which is why a particle has only force equations.
Step 11Rearrange the x-equation: $$F_B=\frac{0.8F_C}{\cos30^{\circ}}=0.9238F_C$$
Step 12Substitute into the y-equation: $$0.9238F_C(0.5)+0.6F_C=735.75\ \mathrm{N}$$
Step 13Collect terms: $$1.0619F_C=735.75\ \mathrm{N}$$
Step 14Solve for $F_C$: $$F_C=\frac{735.75\ \mathrm{N}}{1.0619}=692.9\ \mathrm{N}\approx693\ \mathrm{N}\ \text{(tension)}$$
Step 15Check reasonableness: $F_B=0.9238(692.9)=640\ \mathrm{N}$. Vertical check: $640(0.5)+692.9(0.6)=320+416=736\ \mathrm{N}=W$. Both forces are positive, so both ropes are in tension.
Worked Solution
Free-body diagram of knot A
**Given:** $m=75\ \mathrm{kg}$; rope $AB$ at $30^{\circ}$; rope $AC$ on a 3-4-5 slope. **Find:** $F_C$ (force in $AC$). **FBD at $A$:** $F_B$, $F_C$, and $W=75(9.81)=735.75\ \mathrm{N}$. $$\rightarrow^{+}\ \sum F_x=-F_B\cos30^{\circ}+F_C\left(\tfrac45\right)=0$$ $$\uparrow^{+}\ \sum F_y=F_B\sin30^{\circ}+F_C\left(\tfrac35\right)-735.75\ \mathrm{N}=0$$ From the x-equation $F_B=\dfrac{0.8F_C}{\cos30^{\circ}}=0.9238F_C$. Substituting into the y-equation: $0.9238F_C(0.5)+0.6F_C=735.75$, so $1.0619F_C=735.75$ and $$F_C=692.9\ \mathrm{N}\approx693\ \mathrm{N},\qquad F_B=0.9238(692.9)=640\ \mathrm{N}.$$
Problem 3
Ch. 3 · Q3 — Lamp on a two-joint cable system
A $30\ \mathrm{kg}$ lamp hangs from joint $D$ of a cable system. Cable $DE$ rises to the right from $D$ at $30^{\circ}$ above the horizontal to a wall at $E$. Cable $CD$ is horizontal and connects $D$ to ring $C$ on its left. At ring $C$, cable $AC$ rises to the left on a slope of 4 vertical to 3 horizontal (3-4-5 triangle) to the ceiling at $A$, and cable $BC$ runs down and to the left at $45^{\circ}$ from the vertical to a floor anchor $B$. Take $g=9.81\ \mathrm{m/s^2}$.
Lamp suspended at D with cables DE, CD, AC and BC
Determine the force in cable $BC$.
Solution
412 N
Free-body diagram
Free-body diagrams of joints D and C
Step 1Draw the free-body diagram of joint $D$: isolate $D$. Forces: $F_{DE}$ up-right at $30^{\circ}$ along cable $DE$, $F_{CD}$ horizontally left along cable $CD$, and the lamp weight $W$ straight down.
Step 2List knowns and unknowns: known $m=30\ \mathrm{kg}$, $g=9.81\ \mathrm{m/s^2}$, angles $30^{\circ}$ and $45^{\circ}$, slope 3-4-5; unknown $F_{DE}$, $F_{CD}$, $F_{AC}$, $F_{BC}$; the target is $F_{BC}$.
Step 3State the model and plan: each joint is a particle in 2-D equilibrium with two equations. Joint $C$ has three unknowns, joint $D$ only two, so start at $D$ and carry $F_{CD}$ over to $C$.
Step 4Set axes: $+x$ to the right and $+y$ upward at both joints.
Step 5Compute the weight: $$W=30\ \mathrm{kg}\cdot9.81\ \mathrm{m/s^2}=294.3\ \mathrm{N}$$
Step 6Resolve $F_{DE}$ into components: $F_{DE}\cos30^{\circ}$ to the right and $F_{DE}\sin30^{\circ}$ upward.
Step 7Sum forces in y at $D$: $$\uparrow^{+}\ \sum F_y=F_{DE}\sin30^{\circ}-W=0$$
Step 8Solve for $F_{DE}$: $$F_{DE}=\frac{294.3\ \mathrm{N}}{0.5}=588.6\ \mathrm{N}$$
Step 9Sum forces in x at $D$: $$\rightarrow^{+}\ \sum F_x=F_{DE}\cos30^{\circ}-F_{CD}=0\ \Rightarrow\ F_{CD}=588.6(0.8660)=509.7\ \mathrm{N}$$
Step 10Draw the free-body diagram of ring $C$: isolate $C$. Forces: $F_{CD}=509.7\ \mathrm{N}$ horizontally right (equal and opposite to its pull on $D$), $F_{AC}$ up-left on the 3-4-5 slope, and $F_{BC}$ down-left at $45^{\circ}$ from the vertical.
Step 11Resolve the forces at $C$: $F_{AC}$ has components $\tfrac35F_{AC}$ to the left and $\tfrac45F_{AC}$ upward; $F_{BC}$ has components $F_{BC}\sin45^{\circ}$ to the left and $F_{BC}\cos45^{\circ}$ downward.
Step 12Sum forces in y at $C$: $$\uparrow^{+}\ \sum F_y=\tfrac45F_{AC}-F_{BC}\cos45^{\circ}=0$$
Step 13Sum forces in x at $C$: $$\rightarrow^{+}\ \sum F_x=509.7-F_{BC}\sin45^{\circ}-\tfrac35F_{AC}=0$$
Step 14Eliminate $F_{BC}$: because $\sin45^{\circ}=\cos45^{\circ}$, the y-equation gives $F_{BC}\sin45^{\circ}=0.8F_{AC}$. The x-equation becomes $$509.7=0.8F_{AC}+0.6F_{AC}=1.4F_{AC}\ \Rightarrow\ F_{AC}=364.1\ \mathrm{N}$$
Step 15Solve for $F_{BC}$: $$F_{BC}=\frac{0.8(364.1\ \mathrm{N})}{\cos45^{\circ}}=411.9\ \mathrm{N}\approx412\ \mathrm{N}\ \text{(tension)}$$
Step 16Check: at each joint all forces are concurrent, so $\sum M_D=0$ and $\sum M_C=0$ hold automatically. x-check at $C$: $411.9(0.7071)+364.1(0.6)=291.3+218.5=509.8\ \mathrm{N}\approx F_{CD}$. All forces are positive, so every cable is in tension.
Worked Solution
Free-body diagrams of joints D and C
**Given:** $m=30\ \mathrm{kg}$, geometry as stated. **Find:** $F_{BC}$. **Plan:** solve joint $D$ first (two unknowns), then joint $C$. $W=30(9.81)=294.3\ \mathrm{N}$. **Joint $D$:** $$\uparrow^{+}\ \sum F_y=F_{DE}\sin30^{\circ}-294.3=0\ \Rightarrow\ F_{DE}=588.6\ \mathrm{N}$$ $$\rightarrow^{+}\ \sum F_x=F_{DE}\cos30^{\circ}-F_{CD}=0\ \Rightarrow\ F_{CD}=509.7\ \mathrm{N}$$ **Joint $C$:** $$\uparrow^{+}\ \sum F_y=F_{AC}\left(\tfrac45\right)-F_{BC}\cos45^{\circ}=0$$ $$\rightarrow^{+}\ \sum F_x=509.7-F_{BC}\sin45^{\circ}-F_{AC}\left(\tfrac35\right)=0$$ Since $\sin45^{\circ}=\cos45^{\circ}$, the y-equation gives $F_{BC}\sin45^{\circ}=0.8F_{AC}$; then $509.7=1.4F_{AC}$, so $F_{AC}=364.1\ \mathrm{N}$ and $$F_{BC}=\frac{0.8(364.1)}{\cos45^{\circ}}=411.9\ \mathrm{N}\approx412\ \mathrm{N}.$$
Problem 4
Ch. 3 · Q4 — Simple spring supporting a hanging load
An $8\ \mathrm{kg}$ lamp hangs at rest from the lower end $A$ of a vertical spring whose upper end $B$ is fixed to the ceiling. The spring has stiffness $k=400\ \mathrm{N/m}$ and an unstretched length of $l_0=0.300\ \mathrm{m}$. Take $g=9.81\ \mathrm{m/s^2}$.
Lamp hanging from a vertical spring AB
Determine the stretched length $l$ of the spring.
Solution
0.496 m
Free-body diagram
Free-body diagram of point A
Step 1Draw the free-body diagram: isolate point $A$ at the bottom of the spring. Two forces act: the spring force $F_s$ pulling straight up and the lamp weight $W$ pulling straight down.
Step 2List knowns and unknowns: known $m=8\ \mathrm{kg}$, $k=400\ \mathrm{N/m}$, $l_0=0.300\ \mathrm{m}$, $g=9.81\ \mathrm{m/s^2}$; unknown stretch $s$ and stretched length $l$.
Step 3State the model: point $A$ is a particle at rest; the spring is linear elastic and its own weight is neglected.
Step 4Set the axis: $+y$ upward. No force has a horizontal component, so $\sum F_x=0$ is satisfied identically.
Step 5Compute the weight: $$W=8\ \mathrm{kg}\cdot9.81\ \mathrm{m/s^2}=78.48\ \mathrm{N}$$
Step 6Sum forces in y: $$\uparrow^{+}\ \sum F_y=F_s-W=0$$
Step 7Solve for the spring force: $$F_s=W=78.48\ \mathrm{N}$$
Step 8Check moments: every force on the free body passes through point $A$, so each moment arm is zero and $\sum M_{A}=0$ is satisfied automatically; it gives no new equation, which is why a particle has only force equations.
Step 9Write the spring law: $F_s=ks$, where $s$ is the deformation measured from the unstretched length.
Step 10Rearrange for the stretch: $$s=\frac{F_s}{k}$$
Step 11Substitute numbers: $$s=\frac{78.48\ \mathrm{N}}{400\ \mathrm{N/m}}=0.1962\ \mathrm{m}$$
Step 12Add the stretch to the unstretched length: $$l=l_0+s=0.300\ \mathrm{m}+0.1962\ \mathrm{m}=0.496\ \mathrm{m}$$
Step 13Check reasonableness: the spring is in tension, so it must be longer than $0.300\ \mathrm{m}$; a stretch of about $0.2\ \mathrm{m}$ under roughly $80\ \mathrm{N}$ matches $400\ \mathrm{N/m}$. Units: $\mathrm{N/(N/m)=m}$.
Worked Solution
Free-body diagram of point A
**Given:** $m=8\ \mathrm{kg}$, $k=400\ \mathrm{N/m}$, $l_0=0.300\ \mathrm{m}$. **Find:** $l$. **FBD at $A$:** spring force $F_s$ up, weight $W=8(9.81)=78.48\ \mathrm{N}$ down. $$\uparrow^{+}\ \sum F_y=F_s-78.48\ \mathrm{N}=0\ \Rightarrow\ F_s=78.48\ \mathrm{N}$$ Spring law $F_s=ks$: $$s=\frac{F_s}{k}=\frac{78.48\ \mathrm{N}}{400\ \mathrm{N/m}}=0.1962\ \mathrm{m}$$ $$l=l_0+s=0.300+0.1962=0.496\ \mathrm{m}.$$
Problem 5
Ch. 3 · Q5 — Spring and inclined cable at a ring
A $20\ \mathrm{kg}$ block hangs from ring $A$. The ring is held by a horizontal spring $AB$ attached to a wall on the left and by cable $AC$, which rises to the right at $40^{\circ}$ above the horizontal. The spring stiffness is $k_{AB}=1.20\ \mathrm{kN/m}$. Take $g=9.81\ \mathrm{m/s^2}$.
Block held at ring A by spring AB and cable AC
Determine the stretch of spring $AB$.
Solution
0.195 m
Free-body diagram
Free-body diagram of ring A
Step 1Draw the free-body diagram: isolate ring $A$. Three forces act: the spring force $F_s$ pulling horizontally left toward $B$, the cable tension $T_{AC}$ pulling up-right at $40^{\circ}$, and the block weight $W$ straight down.
Step 2List knowns and unknowns: known $m=20\ \mathrm{kg}$, $k_{AB}=1.20\ \mathrm{kN/m}$, $40^{\circ}$, $g=9.81\ \mathrm{m/s^2}$; unknown $T_{AC}$, $F_s$ and the stretch $s_{AB}$.
Step 3State the model: ring $A$ is a particle in 2-D equilibrium; the spring is linear and is assumed stretched (in tension).
Step 4Set axes: $+x$ to the right and $+y$ upward.
Step 5Convert units: $$k_{AB}=1.20\ \mathrm{kN/m}=1200\ \mathrm{N/m}$$
Step 6Compute the weight: $$W=20\ \mathrm{kg}\cdot9.81\ \mathrm{m/s^2}=196.2\ \mathrm{N}$$
Step 7Resolve $T_{AC}$ into components: $T_{AC}\cos40^{\circ}$ to the right and $T_{AC}\sin40^{\circ}$ upward.
Step 8Sum forces in y: $$\uparrow^{+}\ \sum F_y=T_{AC}\sin40^{\circ}-W=0$$
Step 9Solve for $T_{AC}$: $$T_{AC}=\frac{196.2\ \mathrm{N}}{\sin40^{\circ}}=305.2\ \mathrm{N}$$
Step 10Sum forces in x: $$\rightarrow^{+}\ \sum F_x=T_{AC}\cos40^{\circ}-F_s=0$$
Step 11Solve for the spring force: $$F_s=305.2\ \mathrm{N}\cdot\cos40^{\circ}=233.8\ \mathrm{N}$$
Step 12Check moments: every force on the free body passes through point $A$, so each moment arm is zero and $\sum M_{A}=0$ is satisfied automatically; it gives no new equation, which is why a particle has only force equations.
Step 13Write the spring law and rearrange: $F_s=k_{AB}s_{AB}$, so $$s_{AB}=\frac{F_s}{k_{AB}}$$
Step 14Substitute numbers: $$s_{AB}=\frac{233.8\ \mathrm{N}}{1200\ \mathrm{N/m}}=0.195\ \mathrm{m}$$
Step 15Check reasonableness: $F_s>0$ confirms the spring is stretched, by about $195\ \mathrm{mm}$. Units: $\mathrm{N/(N/m)=m}$.
Worked Solution
Free-body diagram of ring A
**Given:** $m=20\ \mathrm{kg}$, $k_{AB}=1.20\ \mathrm{kN/m}=1200\ \mathrm{N/m}$, cable $AC$ at $40^{\circ}$. **Find:** stretch $s_{AB}$. **FBD at $A$:** $F_s$ (left), $T_{AC}$ (up-right), $W=20(9.81)=196.2\ \mathrm{N}$ (down). $$\uparrow^{+}\ \sum F_y=T_{AC}\sin40^{\circ}-196.2=0\ \Rightarrow\ T_{AC}=305.2\ \mathrm{N}$$ $$\rightarrow^{+}\ \sum F_x=T_{AC}\cos40^{\circ}-F_s=0\ \Rightarrow\ F_s=305.2\cos40^{\circ}=233.8\ \mathrm{N}$$ Spring law: $$s_{AB}=\frac{F_s}{k_{AB}}=\frac{233.8\ \mathrm{N}}{1200\ \mathrm{N/m}}=0.195\ \mathrm{m}.$$
Problem 6
Ch. 3 · Q6 — Largest load limited by cable strength
A crate is to be hung from ring $A$, which is supported by two cables. Cable $AB$ rises to the left at $30^{\circ}$ above the horizontal and can safely carry at most $1.80\ \mathrm{kN}$. Cable $AC$ rises to the right at $45^{\circ}$ above the horizontal and can safely carry at most $2.00\ \mathrm{kN}$. Take $g=9.81\ \mathrm{m/s^2}$.
Crate hung from ring A by cables AB and AC
Determine the largest crate mass $m$ that can be supported without exceeding either cable limit.
Solution
227 kg
Free-body diagram
Free-body diagram of ring A
Step 1Draw the free-body diagram: isolate ring $A$. Three forces act: $T_{AB}$ up-left at $30^{\circ}$, $T_{AC}$ up-right at $45^{\circ}$, and the crate weight $W=mg$ straight down.
Step 2List knowns and unknowns: known limits $T_{AB}\le1.80\ \mathrm{kN}=1800\ \mathrm{N}$ and $T_{AC}\le2.00\ \mathrm{kN}=2000\ \mathrm{N}$, angles $30^{\circ}$ and $45^{\circ}$; unknown the largest $W$, hence $m$.
Step 3State the model and plan: ring $A$ is a particle in 2-D equilibrium. Express both tensions as multiples of $W$, then see which cable reaches its limit first.
Step 4Set axes: $+x$ to the right and $+y$ upward.
Step 5Resolve $T_{AB}$ into components: $-T_{AB}\cos30^{\circ}$ in x (left) and $T_{AB}\sin30^{\circ}$ in y (up).
Step 6Resolve $T_{AC}$ into components: $T_{AC}\cos45^{\circ}$ in x (right) and $T_{AC}\sin45^{\circ}$ in y (up).
Step 7Sum forces in x: $$\rightarrow^{+}\ \sum F_x=-T_{AB}\cos30^{\circ}+T_{AC}\cos45^{\circ}=0$$
Step 8Sum forces in y: $$\uparrow^{+}\ \sum F_y=T_{AB}\sin30^{\circ}+T_{AC}\sin45^{\circ}-W=0$$
Step 9Check moments: every force on the free body passes through point $A$, so each moment arm is zero and $\sum M_{A}=0$ is satisfied automatically; it gives no new equation, which is why a particle has only force equations.
Step 10Rearrange the x-equation: $$T_{AB}=T_{AC}\frac{\cos45^{\circ}}{\cos30^{\circ}}=0.8165\,T_{AC}$$
Step 11Substitute into the y-equation and solve for $T_{AC}$: $$T_{AC}\left[0.8165(0.5)+0.7071\right]=W\ \Rightarrow\ T_{AC}=\frac{W}{1.1154}=0.8966\,W$$
Step 12Back-substitute for $T_{AB}$: $$T_{AB}=0.8165(0.8966\,W)=0.7321\,W$$
Step 13Apply the limit on cable $AB$: $$0.7321\,W\le1800\ \mathrm{N}\ \Rightarrow\ W\le2459\ \mathrm{N}$$
Step 14Apply the limit on cable $AC$: $$0.8966\,W\le2000\ \mathrm{N}\ \Rightarrow\ W\le2231\ \mathrm{N}$$
Step 15Select the governing case and convert to mass: the smaller value controls, so cable $AC$ governs and $$m=\frac{2231\ \mathrm{N}}{9.81\ \mathrm{m/s^2}}=227\ \mathrm{kg}$$
Step 16Check: at $W=2231\ \mathrm{N}$, $T_{AC}=2000\ \mathrm{N}$ (at its limit) and $T_{AB}=0.7321(2231)=1633\ \mathrm{N}<1800\ \mathrm{N}$. The steeper cable $AC$ carries more of the load, as expected. Units: $\mathrm{N/(m/s^2)=kg}$.
Worked Solution
Free-body diagram of ring A
**Given:** $T_{AB}\le1800\ \mathrm{N}$ at $30^{\circ}$, $T_{AC}\le2000\ \mathrm{N}$ at $45^{\circ}$. **Find:** largest $m$. **FBD at $A$:** $T_{AB}$, $T_{AC}$, $W=mg$. $$\rightarrow^{+}\ \sum F_x=-T_{AB}\cos30^{\circ}+T_{AC}\cos45^{\circ}=0$$ $$\uparrow^{+}\ \sum F_y=T_{AB}\sin30^{\circ}+T_{AC}\sin45^{\circ}-W=0$$ From the x-equation $T_{AB}=T_{AC}\dfrac{\cos45^{\circ}}{\cos30^{\circ}}=0.8165T_{AC}$. Then $T_{AC}(0.4082+0.7071)=W$, so $T_{AC}=0.8966W$ and $T_{AB}=0.7321W$. Limits: $W\le\dfrac{1800}{0.7321}=2459\ \mathrm{N}$ (cable $AB$) and $W\le\dfrac{2000}{0.8966}=2231\ \mathrm{N}$ (cable $AC$). Cable $AC$ governs: $$m=\frac{2231\ \mathrm{N}}{9.81\ \mathrm{m/s^2}}=227\ \mathrm{kg}.$$ At this load $T_{AB}=0.7321(2231)=1633\ \mathrm{N}<1800\ \mathrm{N}$.
Problem 7
Ch. 3 · Q7 — Load on a frictionless pulley riding a cable
A $40\ \mathrm{kg}$ bucket hangs from a small frictionless pulley $A$ that is free to roll on a continuous cable strung between wall anchors $B$ (left) and $C$ (right). In the rest position each segment of the cable makes $20^{\circ}$ with the horizontal. Take $g=9.81\ \mathrm{m/s^2}$.
Bucket on a frictionless pulley riding cable BAC
Determine the tension in the cable.
Solution
574 N
Free-body diagram
Free-body diagram of pulley A
Step 1Draw the free-body diagram: isolate pulley $A$ together with the short piece of cable wrapped on it. Forces: cable tension pulling up-left toward $B$, cable tension pulling up-right toward $C$, and the bucket weight $W$ straight down.
Step 2List knowns and unknowns: known $m=40\ \mathrm{kg}$, $g=9.81\ \mathrm{m/s^2}$, both angles $20^{\circ}$; unknown the cable tension.
Step 3State the model: the pulley is small (a particle) and frictionless, and the cable is continuous, so the tension is the same on both sides: $T_1=T_2=T$.
Step 4Set axes: $+x$ to the right and $+y$ upward.
Step 5Compute the weight: $$W=40\ \mathrm{kg}\cdot9.81\ \mathrm{m/s^2}=392.4\ \mathrm{N}$$
Step 6Resolve the left segment: components $-T\cos20^{\circ}$ in x and $T\sin20^{\circ}$ in y.
Step 7Resolve the right segment: components $+T\cos20^{\circ}$ in x and $T\sin20^{\circ}$ in y.
Step 8Sum forces in x: $$\rightarrow^{+}\ \sum F_x=T\cos20^{\circ}-T\cos20^{\circ}=0$$ This is satisfied identically, which is why the two angles must be equal.
Step 9Sum forces in y: $$\uparrow^{+}\ \sum F_y=2T\sin20^{\circ}-W=0$$
Step 10Check moments: every force on the free body passes through point $A$, so each moment arm is zero and $\sum M_{A}=0$ is satisfied automatically; it gives no new equation, which is why a particle has only force equations.
Step 11Rearrange: $$T=\frac{W}{2\sin20^{\circ}}$$
Step 12Substitute numbers: $$T=\frac{392.4\ \mathrm{N}}{2(0.3420)}=573.7\ \mathrm{N}$$
Step 13State the result: the cable tension is $T\approx574\ \mathrm{N}$ throughout the cable.
Step 14Check reasonableness: $T>W$ because the cable is shallow and only $\sin20^{\circ}\approx34\%$ of each tension acts vertically; a flatter cable would need an even larger tension.
Worked Solution
Free-body diagram of pulley A
**Given:** $m=40\ \mathrm{kg}$, both cable segments at $20^{\circ}$. **Find:** $T$. For a frictionless pulley and cable, $T_1=T_2=T$. **FBD at $A$:** $T$ up-left, $T$ up-right, $W=40(9.81)=392.4\ \mathrm{N}$ down. $$\rightarrow^{+}\ \sum F_x=T\cos20^{\circ}-T\cos20^{\circ}=0\ \ (\text{satisfied})$$ $$\uparrow^{+}\ \sum F_y=2T\sin20^{\circ}-392.4\ \mathrm{N}=0$$ $$T=\frac{392.4\ \mathrm{N}}{2\sin20^{\circ}}=573.7\ \mathrm{N}\approx574\ \mathrm{N}.$$
Problem 8
Ch. 3 · Q8 — Cylinder on a smooth incline held by a cord
A $30\ \mathrm{kg}$ cylinder rests on a smooth plane inclined at $25^{\circ}$ to the horizontal. It is held in place by a cord attached at its centre $O$ and tied to a hook uphill; the cord makes an angle of $15^{\circ}$ with the incline, rising away from the surface. Take $g=9.81\ \mathrm{m/s^2}$.
Cylinder on a smooth incline restrained by a cord
Determine the tension in the cord.
Solution
129 N
Free-body diagram
Free-body diagram of the cylinder
Step 1Draw the free-body diagram: isolate the cylinder from the incline and the cord. Forces: weight $W$ straight down through $O$, normal force $N$ from the smooth surface perpendicular to the incline through $O$, and cord tension $T$ pulling from $O$ up the slope at $15^{\circ}$ to the incline.
Step 2List knowns and unknowns: known $m=30\ \mathrm{kg}$, $g=9.81\ \mathrm{m/s^2}$, incline $25^{\circ}$, cord angle $15^{\circ}$; unknown $T$ and $N$.
Step 3State the model: the surface is smooth, so it exerts only a normal force (no friction). The three forces are concurrent at $O$, so the cylinder can be treated as a particle.
Step 4Set axes: $+x$ along the incline pointing uphill and $+y$ perpendicular to the incline, away from the surface. This puts the unknown $N$ entirely on the y-axis.
Step 5Compute the weight: $$W=30\ \mathrm{kg}\cdot9.81\ \mathrm{m/s^2}=294.3\ \mathrm{N}$$
Step 6Resolve the weight: $W\sin25^{\circ}$ down the slope ($-x$) and $W\cos25^{\circ}$ into the surface ($-y$).
Step 7Resolve the tension: $T\cos15^{\circ}$ up the slope ($+x$) and $T\sin15^{\circ}$ away from the surface ($+y$).
Step 8Sum forces in x: $$\sum F_x=T\cos15^{\circ}-W\sin25^{\circ}=0$$ $N$ does not appear, so this equation has one unknown.
Step 9Sum forces in y: $$\sum F_y=N+T\sin15^{\circ}-W\cos25^{\circ}=0$$
Step 10Check moments: every force on the free body passes through point $O$, so each moment arm is zero and $\sum M_{O}=0$ is satisfied automatically; it gives no new equation, which is why a particle has only force equations.
Step 11Rearrange the x-equation: $$T=\frac{W\sin25^{\circ}}{\cos15^{\circ}}$$
Step 12Substitute numbers: $$T=\frac{294.3\ \mathrm{N}\,(0.4226)}{0.9659}=128.8\ \mathrm{N}$$
Step 13State the result: the cord tension is $T\approx129\ \mathrm{N}$.
Step 14Check reasonableness: the y-equation gives $N=294.3(0.9063)-128.8(0.2588)=233\ \mathrm{N}>0$, so the cylinder stays in contact. $T$ is well below $W$ because the incline carries most of the weight.
Worked Solution
Free-body diagram of the cylinder
**Given:** $m=30\ \mathrm{kg}$, incline $25^{\circ}$, cord at $15^{\circ}$ to the incline, smooth contact. **Find:** $T$. **FBD of cylinder:** $W=30(9.81)=294.3\ \mathrm{N}$ (down), $N$ (normal to the incline), $T$ (along the cord); all three are concurrent at $O$, so the cylinder is treated as a particle. Axes: $x$ up the incline, $y$ normal to it. $$\nearrow^{+}\ \sum F_x=T\cos15^{\circ}-294.3\sin25^{\circ}=0$$ $$\nwarrow^{+}\ \sum F_y=N+T\sin15^{\circ}-294.3\cos25^{\circ}=0$$ $$T=\frac{294.3\sin25^{\circ}}{\cos15^{\circ}}=\frac{124.4}{0.9659}=128.8\ \mathrm{N}\approx129\ \mathrm{N}.$$ Then $N=266.7-128.8(0.2588)=233\ \mathrm{N}$.
Problem 9
Ch. 3 · Q9 — Equilibrium angle with two pulley counterweights
A $40\ \mathrm{kg}$ load $E$ hangs from ring $A$. Cord $AB$ runs up and to the left from $A$, passes over a frictionless pulley at $B$ and carries a $25\ \mathrm{kg}$ block. Cord $AC$ runs up and to the right from $A$, passes over a frictionless pulley at $C$ and carries a $30\ \mathrm{kg}$ block. In the equilibrium position cord $AB$ makes an angle $\alpha$ with the horizontal and cord $AC$ makes an angle $\beta$ with the horizontal. Take $g=9.81\ \mathrm{m/s^2}$.
Ring A in equilibrium between two pulley counterweights
Determine the angle $\alpha$ for equilibrium.
Solution
41.5 deg
Free-body diagram
Free-body diagram of ring A
Step 1Draw the free-body diagram: isolate ring $A$. Forces: $T_B$ along cord $AB$ up-left at angle $\alpha$, $T_C$ along cord $AC$ up-right at angle $\beta$, and the load weight $W$ straight down.
Step 2List knowns and unknowns: known masses $25\ \mathrm{kg}$, $30\ \mathrm{kg}$ and $40\ \mathrm{kg}$, $g=9.81\ \mathrm{m/s^2}$; unknown angles $\alpha$ and $\beta$. Here the force magnitudes are known and the directions are the unknowns.
Step 3State the model: ring $A$ is a particle in 2-D equilibrium. Each pulley is frictionless, so the tension in each cord equals the weight of the block hanging from it.
Step 4Set axes: $+x$ to the right and $+y$ upward.
Step 5Compute the force magnitudes: $$T_B=25(9.81)=245.25\ \mathrm{N},\quad T_C=30(9.81)=294.3\ \mathrm{N},\quad W=40(9.81)=392.4\ \mathrm{N}$$
Step 6Resolve $T_B$ into components: $-T_B\cos\alpha$ in x and $T_B\sin\alpha$ in y.
Step 7Resolve $T_C$ into components: $T_C\cos\beta$ in x and $T_C\sin\beta$ in y.
Step 8Sum forces in x: $$\rightarrow^{+}\ \sum F_x=-T_B\cos\alpha+T_C\cos\beta=0$$
Step 9Sum forces in y: $$\uparrow^{+}\ \sum F_y=T_B\sin\alpha+T_C\sin\beta-W=0$$
Step 10Check moments: every force on the free body passes through point $A$, so each moment arm is zero and $\sum M_{A}=0$ is satisfied automatically; it gives no new equation, which is why a particle has only force equations.
Step 11Isolate the $\beta$ terms: $$T_C\cos\beta=T_B\cos\alpha,\qquad T_C\sin\beta=W-T_B\sin\alpha$$
Step 12Square and add to eliminate $\beta$ (using $\sin^2+\cos^2=1$): $$T_C^2=T_B^2+W^2-2T_BW\sin\alpha$$
Step 13Rearrange for $\sin\alpha$: $$\sin\alpha=\frac{T_B^2+W^2-T_C^2}{2T_BW}$$
Step 14Substitute numbers ($g$ cancels, so the masses can be used directly): $$\sin\alpha=\frac{25^2+40^2-30^2}{2(25)(40)}=\frac{1325}{2000}=0.6625$$
Step 15Solve for the angle: $$\alpha=\sin^{-1}(0.6625)=41.5^{\circ}$$
Step 16Check: $\cos\beta=25\cos41.5^{\circ}/30=0.624$ gives $\beta=51.4^{\circ}$; vertical check in mass units: $25\sin41.5^{\circ}+30\sin51.4^{\circ}=16.6+23.4=40.0$. The heavier counterweight pulls its cord steeper, as expected.
Worked Solution
Free-body diagram of ring A
**Given:** masses $25\ \mathrm{kg}$, $30\ \mathrm{kg}$, $40\ \mathrm{kg}$; frictionless pulleys. **Find:** $\alpha$. Each cord tension equals the weight it carries: $T_B=25(9.81)=245.25\ \mathrm{N}$, $T_C=30(9.81)=294.3\ \mathrm{N}$, $W=40(9.81)=392.4\ \mathrm{N}$. **FBD at $A$:** $$\rightarrow^{+}\ \sum F_x=-T_B\cos\alpha+T_C\cos\beta=0$$ $$\uparrow^{+}\ \sum F_y=T_B\sin\alpha+T_C\sin\beta-W=0$$ Isolate the $\beta$ terms, $T_C\cos\beta=T_B\cos\alpha$ and $T_C\sin\beta=W-T_B\sin\alpha$, then square and add: $$T_C^2=T_B^2+W^2-2T_BW\sin\alpha$$ $$\sin\alpha=\frac{T_B^2+W^2-T_C^2}{2T_BW}=\frac{25^2+40^2-30^2}{2(25)(40)}=0.6625$$ ($g$ cancels.) $$\alpha=\sin^{-1}(0.6625)=41.5^{\circ}.$$ Check: $\cos\beta=\dfrac{25\cos41.5^{\circ}}{30}=0.624$, $\beta=51.4^{\circ}$.
Problem 10
Ch. 3 · Q10 — Balancing force for a 3-D particle
Four forces act on particle $A$, which is in equilibrium. Three of them are known: $\mathbf{F}_1=\{200\mathbf{i}+100\mathbf{j}-300\mathbf{k}\}\ \mathrm{N}$, $\mathbf{F}_2=\{-150\mathbf{i}+250\mathbf{j}+100\mathbf{k}\}\ \mathrm{N}$ and $\mathbf{F}_3=\{50\mathbf{i}-400\mathbf{j}+450\mathbf{k}\}\ \mathrm{N}$. The fourth force is $\mathbf{P}$.
Particle A acted on by F1, F2, F3 and P
Determine the magnitude of $\mathbf{P}$.
Solution
274 N
Free-body diagram
Free-body diagram of particle A
Step 1Draw the free-body diagram: isolate particle $A$ and show the four forces acting on it, $\mathbf{F}_1$, $\mathbf{F}_2$, $\mathbf{F}_3$ and the unknown $\mathbf{P}$, each as an arrow from $A$ with x, y, z axes at $A$.
Step 2List knowns and unknowns: known the Cartesian components of $\mathbf{F}_1$, $\mathbf{F}_2$, $\mathbf{F}_3$ in newtons; unknown $\mathbf{P}=P_x\mathbf{i}+P_y\mathbf{j}+P_z\mathbf{k}$, three unknowns.
Step 3State the model: $A$ is a particle in 3-D equilibrium, so three scalar equations are available, enough for the three unknown components.
Step 4Write the vector equation of equilibrium: $$\sum\mathbf{F}=\mathbf{F}_1+\mathbf{F}_2+\mathbf{F}_3+\mathbf{P}=\mathbf{0}$$
Step 5Sum forces in x: $$\sum F_x=200-150+50+P_x=0$$
Step 6Solve for $P_x$: $$P_x=-100\ \mathrm{N}$$
Step 7Sum forces in y: $$\sum F_y=100+250-400+P_y=0$$
Step 8Solve for $P_y$: $$P_y=50\ \mathrm{N}$$
Step 9Sum forces in z: $$\sum F_z=-300+100+450+P_z=0$$
Step 10Solve for $P_z$: $$P_z=-250\ \mathrm{N}$$
Step 11Assemble the vector: $$\mathbf{P}=\{-100\mathbf{i}+50\mathbf{j}-250\mathbf{k}\}\ \mathrm{N}$$
Step 12Write the magnitude formula: $$P=\sqrt{P_x^2+P_y^2+P_z^2}$$
Step 13Substitute numbers: $$P=\sqrt{(-100)^2+(50)^2+(-250)^2}\ \mathrm{N}=\sqrt{75\,000}\ \mathrm{N}=273.9\ \mathrm{N}\approx274\ \mathrm{N}$$
Step 14Check: adding all four vectors gives $0\mathbf{i}+0\mathbf{j}+0\mathbf{k}$, as equilibrium requires. All forces pass through $A$, so $\sum M_A=0$ is satisfied automatically. $\mathbf{P}$ is equal and opposite to the resultant of the other three.
Worked Solution
Free-body diagram of particle A
**Given:** $\mathbf{F}_1$, $\mathbf{F}_2$, $\mathbf{F}_3$ as stated. **Find:** $P$. Equilibrium: $\sum\mathbf{F}=\mathbf{F}_1+\mathbf{F}_2+\mathbf{F}_3+\mathbf{P}=\mathbf{0}$. $$\sum F_x=200-150+50+P_x=0\ \Rightarrow\ P_x=-100\ \mathrm{N}$$ $$\sum F_y=100+250-400+P_y=0\ \Rightarrow\ P_y=50\ \mathrm{N}$$ $$\sum F_z=-300+100+450+P_z=0\ \Rightarrow\ P_z=-250\ \mathrm{N}$$ $\mathbf{P}=\{-100\mathbf{i}+50\mathbf{j}-250\mathbf{k}\}\ \mathrm{N}$ and $$P=\sqrt{(-100)^2+50^2+(-250)^2}=\sqrt{75\,000}=274\ \mathrm{N}.$$
Problem 11
Ch. 3 · Q11 — Three cords supporting a load in 3-D
An $80\ \mathrm{kg}$ load hangs from ring $A$, located at the origin of an $x,y,z$ frame with $z$ vertical (up). Three cords hold the ring: cord $AC$ lies along the negative $x$ axis; cord $AB$ lies in the horizontal $x$-$y$ plane at $40^{\circ}$ from the positive $y$ axis, measured toward the positive $x$ axis; cord $AD$ runs to the ceiling point $D(2,\,-3,\,6)\ \mathrm{m}$. Take $g=9.81\ \mathrm{m/s^2}$.
Load at ring A supported by cords AB, AC and AD
Determine the tension in cord $AC$.
Solution
591 N
Free-body diagram
Free-body diagram of ring A
Step 1Draw the free-body diagram: isolate ring $A$. Four forces act: $\mathbf{F}_C$ along $-x$, $\mathbf{F}_B$ in the $x$-$y$ plane at $40^{\circ}$ from $+y$, $\mathbf{F}_D$ directed from $A$ toward $D$, and the weight $\mathbf{W}$ along $-z$.
Step 2List knowns and unknowns: known $m=80\ \mathrm{kg}$, $g=9.81\ \mathrm{m/s^2}$, $D(2,-3,6)\ \mathrm{m}$, angle $40^{\circ}$; unknown magnitudes $F_B$, $F_C$, $F_D$ (three unknowns, three equations).
Step 3State the model: ring $A$ is a particle in 3-D equilibrium; each cord is in tension and acts along its own line, so every direction is known.
Step 4Compute the weight: $$W=80\ \mathrm{kg}\cdot9.81\ \mathrm{m/s^2}=784.8\ \mathrm{N},\qquad \mathbf{W}=-784.8\mathbf{k}\ \mathrm{N}$$
Step 5Write $\mathbf{F}_B$ in Cartesian form: $$\mathbf{F}_B=F_B(\sin40^{\circ}\mathbf{i}+\cos40^{\circ}\mathbf{j})=0.6428F_B\mathbf{i}+0.7660F_B\mathbf{j}$$
Step 6Write $\mathbf{F}_C$ in Cartesian form: $$\mathbf{F}_C=-F_C\mathbf{i}$$
Step 7Find the unit vector from $A$ to $D$: $$\mathbf{r}_{AD}=\{2\mathbf{i}-3\mathbf{j}+6\mathbf{k}\}\ \mathrm{m},\quad r_{AD}=\sqrt{2^2+3^2+6^2}=7\ \mathrm{m}$$
Step 8Write $\mathbf{F}_D$ in Cartesian form: $$\mathbf{F}_D=F_D\frac{\mathbf{r}_{AD}}{r_{AD}}=\tfrac27F_D\mathbf{i}-\tfrac37F_D\mathbf{j}+\tfrac67F_D\mathbf{k}$$
Step 9Sum forces in z: $$\sum F_z=\tfrac67F_D-784.8\ \mathrm{N}=0$$ Start here because only $F_D$ has a z-component.
Step 10Solve for $F_D$: $$F_D=\tfrac76(784.8\ \mathrm{N})=915.6\ \mathrm{N}$$
Step 11Sum forces in y: $$\sum F_y=F_B\cos40^{\circ}-\tfrac37F_D=0$$
Step 12Solve for $F_B$: $$F_B=\frac{\tfrac37(915.6\ \mathrm{N})}{\cos40^{\circ}}=\frac{392.4\ \mathrm{N}}{0.7660}=512.2\ \mathrm{N}$$
Step 13Sum forces in x: $$\sum F_x=F_B\sin40^{\circ}-F_C+\tfrac27F_D=0$$
Step 14Solve for $F_C$: $$F_C=512.2(0.6428)+\tfrac27(915.6)=329.3+261.6=590.9\ \mathrm{N}\approx591\ \mathrm{N}$$
Step 15Check: all three magnitudes are positive, so every cord is in tension as assumed. All forces pass through $A$, so $\sum M_A=0$ holds automatically. $F_D>W$ because cord $AD$ alone supplies the vertical support while also pulling sideways.
Worked Solution
Free-body diagram of ring A
**Given:** $m=80\ \mathrm{kg}$, $D(2,-3,6)\ \mathrm{m}$, cord $AB$ at $40^{\circ}$ from $+y$ in the $x$-$y$ plane. **Find:** $F_C$. $W=80(9.81)=784.8\ \mathrm{N}$. Cartesian vectors: $$\mathbf{F}_B=F_B(\sin40^{\circ}\mathbf{i}+\cos40^{\circ}\mathbf{j}),\quad \mathbf{F}_C=-F_C\mathbf{i},\quad \mathbf{W}=-784.8\mathbf{k}\ \mathrm{N}$$ $$\mathbf{F}_D=F_D\frac{\mathbf{r}_{AD}}{r_{AD}}=F_D\frac{2\mathbf{i}-3\mathbf{j}+6\mathbf{k}}{\sqrt{2^2+3^2+6^2}}=F_D\left(\tfrac27\mathbf{i}-\tfrac37\mathbf{j}+\tfrac67\mathbf{k}\right)$$ $$\sum F_z=\tfrac67F_D-784.8=0\ \Rightarrow\ F_D=915.6\ \mathrm{N}$$ $$\sum F_y=F_B\cos40^{\circ}-\tfrac37F_D=0\ \Rightarrow\ F_B=\frac{392.4}{0.7660}=512.2\ \mathrm{N}$$ $$\sum F_x=F_B\sin40^{\circ}-F_C+\tfrac27F_D=0\ \Rightarrow\ F_C=329.3+261.6=590.9\ \mathrm{N}\approx591\ \mathrm{N}.$$
Problem 12
Ch. 3 · Q12 — Crate held by two cables and a strut in 3-D
A $150\ \mathrm{kg}$ crate hangs from joint $A$, located at the origin of an $x,y,z$ frame with $z$ vertical (up). Joint $A$ is held by cable $AB$ to wall point $B(-4,\,-12,\,3)\ \mathrm{m}$, by cable $AC$ to wall point $C(2,\,-6,\,3)\ \mathrm{m}$, and by strut $AD$, whose other end is pinned at $D(0,\,-12,\,-5)\ \mathrm{m}$. The strut pushes on joint $A$ along its own axis, directed from $D$ toward $A$. Take $g=9.81\ \mathrm{m/s^2}$.
Crate at joint A held by cables AB, AC and strut AD
Determine the magnitude of the force developed along strut $AD$.
Solution
2010 N
Free-body diagram
Free-body diagram of joint A
Step 1Draw the free-body diagram: isolate joint $A$. Four forces act: cable tension $\mathbf{F}_B$ directed from $A$ toward $B$, cable tension $\mathbf{F}_C$ directed from $A$ toward $C$, strut force $\mathbf{F}_D$ pushing on $A$ along the line from $D$ to $A$, and the crate weight $\mathbf{W}$ along $-z$.
Step 2List knowns and unknowns: known $m=150\ \mathrm{kg}$, $g=9.81\ \mathrm{m/s^2}$ and the coordinates of $B$, $C$, $D$; unknown magnitudes $F_B$, $F_C$, $F_D$.
Step 3State the model: joint $A$ is a particle in 3-D equilibrium; cables pull along their lines, and the strut is assumed in compression so it pushes on $A$. A negative answer would mean the opposite sense.
Step 4Compute the weight: $$W=150\ \mathrm{kg}\cdot9.81\ \mathrm{m/s^2}=1471.5\ \mathrm{N},\qquad\mathbf{W}=-1471.5\mathbf{k}\ \mathrm{N}$$
Step 5Write $\mathbf{F}_B$ in Cartesian form: $r_{AB}=\sqrt{4^2+12^2+3^2}=13\ \mathrm{m}$, so $$\mathbf{F}_B=F_B\left(-\tfrac{4}{13}\mathbf{i}-\tfrac{12}{13}\mathbf{j}+\tfrac{3}{13}\mathbf{k}\right)$$
Step 6Write $\mathbf{F}_C$ in Cartesian form: $r_{AC}=\sqrt{2^2+6^2+3^2}=7\ \mathrm{m}$, so $$\mathbf{F}_C=F_C\left(\tfrac27\mathbf{i}-\tfrac67\mathbf{j}+\tfrac37\mathbf{k}\right)$$
Step 7Write $\mathbf{F}_D$ in Cartesian form: $\mathbf{r}_{DA}=\{12\mathbf{j}+5\mathbf{k}\}\ \mathrm{m}$, $r_{DA}=13\ \mathrm{m}$, so $$\mathbf{F}_D=F_D\left(\tfrac{12}{13}\mathbf{j}+\tfrac{5}{13}\mathbf{k}\right)$$
Step 8Sum forces in x: $$\sum F_x=-\tfrac{4}{13}F_B+\tfrac27F_C=0\quad(1)$$
Step 9Sum forces in y: $$\sum F_y=-\tfrac{12}{13}F_B-\tfrac67F_C+\tfrac{12}{13}F_D=0\quad(2)$$
Step 10Sum forces in z: $$\sum F_z=\tfrac{3}{13}F_B+\tfrac37F_C+\tfrac{5}{13}F_D-1471.5\ \mathrm{N}=0\quad(3)$$
Step 11Rearrange (1): $$F_C=\tfrac{4}{13}\cdot\tfrac72F_B=\tfrac{14}{13}F_B$$
Step 12Rearrange (2): $$F_D=F_B+\tfrac{13}{14}F_C=F_B+\tfrac{13}{14}\cdot\tfrac{14}{13}F_B=2F_B$$
Step 13Substitute both into (3): $$\tfrac{3}{13}F_B+\tfrac37\cdot\tfrac{14}{13}F_B+\tfrac{5}{13}(2F_B)=\tfrac{19}{13}F_B=1471.5\ \mathrm{N}$$
Step 14Solve for $F_B$: $$F_B=\tfrac{13}{19}(1471.5\ \mathrm{N})=1006.8\ \mathrm{N}$$
Step 15Solve for the strut force: $$F_D=2F_B=2(1006.8\ \mathrm{N})=2014\ \mathrm{N}\approx2010\ \mathrm{N}$$ Positive, so the strut is in compression as assumed.
Step 16Check: $F_C=\tfrac{14}{13}(1006.8)=1084\ \mathrm{N}$; z-check: $232.3+464.7+774.5=1471.5\ \mathrm{N}=W$. All forces are concurrent at $A$, so $\sum M_A=0$ is satisfied automatically.
Worked Solution
Free-body diagram of joint A
**Given:** $m=150\ \mathrm{kg}$; $B(-4,-12,3)$, $C(2,-6,3)$, $D(0,-12,-5)\ \mathrm{m}$; $A$ at the origin. **Find:** $F_D$. $\mathbf{W}=-150(9.81)\mathbf{k}=-1471.5\mathbf{k}\ \mathrm{N}$. $$\mathbf{F}_B=F_B\frac{\mathbf{r}_{AB}}{r_{AB}}=F_B\frac{-4\mathbf{i}-12\mathbf{j}+3\mathbf{k}}{13},\quad \mathbf{F}_C=F_C\frac{2\mathbf{i}-6\mathbf{j}+3\mathbf{k}}{7},\quad \mathbf{F}_D=F_D\frac{\mathbf{r}_{DA}}{r_{DA}}=F_D\frac{12\mathbf{j}+5\mathbf{k}}{13}$$ $$\sum F_x=-\tfrac{4}{13}F_B+\tfrac27F_C=0\quad(1)$$ $$\sum F_y=-\tfrac{12}{13}F_B-\tfrac67F_C+\tfrac{12}{13}F_D=0\quad(2)$$ $$\sum F_z=\tfrac{3}{13}F_B+\tfrac37F_C+\tfrac{5}{13}F_D-1471.5=0\quad(3)$$ From (1): $F_C=\tfrac{14}{13}F_B$. From (2): $F_D=F_B+\tfrac{13}{14}F_C=2F_B$. In (3): $\left(\tfrac{3}{13}+\tfrac{6}{13}+\tfrac{10}{13}\right)F_B=\tfrac{19}{13}F_B=1471.5$, so $F_B=1006.8\ \mathrm{N}$, $F_C=1084\ \mathrm{N}$ and $$F_D=2(1006.8)=2014\ \mathrm{N}\approx2010\ \mathrm{N}\ \text{(compression in the strut)}.$$
Problem 13
Ch. 3 · Q13 — Symmetric three-chain hanger
A $25\ \mathrm{kg}$ planter hangs from ring $A$. Three identical chains $AB$, $AC$ and $AD$, each $1.30\ \mathrm{m}$ long, run from $A$ up to ceiling hooks $B$, $C$ and $D$. The hooks are equally spaced ($120^{\circ}$ apart) on a horizontal circle of radius $0.500\ \mathrm{m}$ whose centre $O$ is directly above $A$. Take $g=9.81\ \mathrm{m/s^2}$.
Planter hung from ring A by three equal chains
Determine the tension in each chain.
Solution
88.6 N
Free-body diagram
Free-body diagram of ring A
Step 1Draw the free-body diagram: isolate ring $A$. Four forces act: the three chain tensions along $AB$, $AC$ and $AD$, each pulling up and outward toward its hook, and the planter weight $W$ straight down.
Step 2List knowns and unknowns: known $m=25\ \mathrm{kg}$, chain length $1.30\ \mathrm{m}$, hook-circle radius $0.500\ \mathrm{m}$, $g=9.81\ \mathrm{m/s^2}$; unknown the chain tensions.
Step 3State the model: ring $A$ is a particle in 3-D equilibrium. The chains are identical and symmetrically placed about the vertical through $A$, so all three carry the same tension $T$.
Step 4Set axes: $z$ vertical (up) through $A$ and $O$; $x$ and $y$ horizontal.
Step 5Compute the weight: $$W=25\ \mathrm{kg}\cdot9.81\ \mathrm{m/s^2}=245.25\ \mathrm{N}$$
Step 6Find the height of the hooks above $A$: $$h=\sqrt{(1.30\ \mathrm{m})^2-(0.500\ \mathrm{m})^2}=1.20\ \mathrm{m}$$
Step 7Resolve one chain tension: vertical component $T_z=T\left(\tfrac{1.20}{1.30}\right)$ and horizontal component $T_h=T\left(\tfrac{0.500}{1.30}\right)$ pointing toward its hook.
Step 8Sum the horizontal forces: the three equal horizontal components are $120^{\circ}$ apart, so they form a closed triangle and $\sum F_x=0$ and $\sum F_y=0$ are satisfied identically.
Step 9Sum forces in z: $$\sum F_z=3T\left(\frac{1.20}{1.30}\right)-W=0$$
Step 10Check moments: every force on the free body passes through point $A$, so each moment arm is zero and $\sum M_{A}=0$ is satisfied automatically; it gives no new equation, which is why a particle has only force equations.
Step 11Rearrange: $$T=\frac{1.30\,W}{3(1.20)}$$
Step 12Substitute numbers: $$T=\frac{1.30(245.25\ \mathrm{N})}{3.60}=88.6\ \mathrm{N}$$
Step 13State the result: each chain carries a tension of $T\approx88.6\ \mathrm{N}$.
Step 14Check reasonableness: three vertical chains would each carry $W/3=81.8\ \mathrm{N}$; the inclined chains must carry slightly more, and $88.6\ \mathrm{N}$ is about $8\%$ higher, consistent with $1.30/1.20$.
Worked Solution
Free-body diagram of ring A
**Given:** $m=25\ \mathrm{kg}$, chain length $1.30\ \mathrm{m}$, hook radius $0.500\ \mathrm{m}$. **Find:** $T$. By symmetry the three tensions are equal. Height of the hooks above $A$: $h=\sqrt{1.30^2-0.500^2}=1.20\ \mathrm{m}$, so each chain has vertical direction cosine $\dfrac{1.20}{1.30}$. The horizontal components, $T\left(\tfrac{0.500}{1.30}\right)$ each at $120^{\circ}$ spacing, cancel, so $\sum F_x=\sum F_y=0$. $W=25(9.81)=245.25\ \mathrm{N}$. $$\sum F_z=3T\left(\frac{1.20}{1.30}\right)-245.25\ \mathrm{N}=0$$ $$T=\frac{245.25(1.30)}{3(1.20)}=88.6\ \mathrm{N}.$$
Problem 14
Ch. 3 · Q14 — Unknown holding force on a ring with three known forces
Ring $A$ is in equilibrium under four coplanar cable forces. Three are known: $F_1=600\ \mathrm{N}$ acting up and to the right at $20^{\circ}$ above the positive $x$ axis; $F_2=450\ \mathrm{N}$ acting up and to the left at $60^{\circ}$ above the negative $x$ axis; and $F_3=300\ \mathrm{N}$ acting straight down. The fourth cable exerts a force $\mathbf{F}$ of unknown magnitude and direction.
Ring A with three known cable forces and unknown force F
Determine the magnitude of $\mathbf{F}$ required for equilibrium.
Solution
449 N
Free-body diagram
Free-body diagram of ring A
Step 1Draw the free-body diagram: isolate ring $A$. Four forces act: $F_1$ up-right at $20^{\circ}$, $F_2$ up-left at $60^{\circ}$ above the negative $x$ axis, $F_3$ straight down, and the unknown $\mathbf{F}$, drawn as components $F_x$ and $F_y$ assumed positive.
Step 2List knowns and unknowns: known $F_1=600\ \mathrm{N}$, $F_2=450\ \mathrm{N}$, $F_3=300\ \mathrm{N}$ and their directions; unknown $F_x$ and $F_y$, from which the magnitude $F$ follows.
Step 3State the model: ring $A$ is a particle under a coplanar force system; two scalar equations give the two unknown components.
Step 4Set axes: $+x$ to the right and $+y$ upward.
Step 5Resolve $F_1$: $$F_{1x}=600\cos20^{\circ}=563.8\ \mathrm{N},\qquad F_{1y}=600\sin20^{\circ}=205.2\ \mathrm{N}$$
Step 6Resolve $F_2$: $$F_{2x}=-450\cos60^{\circ}=-225.0\ \mathrm{N},\qquad F_{2y}=450\sin60^{\circ}=389.7\ \mathrm{N}$$
Step 7Resolve $F_3$: $F_{3x}=0$ and $F_{3y}=-300\ \mathrm{N}$.
Step 8Sum forces in x: $$\rightarrow^{+}\ \sum F_x=563.8-225.0+F_x=0$$
Step 9Solve for $F_x$: $$F_x=-338.8\ \mathrm{N}$$ The negative sign means it acts to the left.
Step 10Sum forces in y: $$\uparrow^{+}\ \sum F_y=205.2+389.7-300+F_y=0$$
Step 11Solve for $F_y$: $$F_y=-294.9\ \mathrm{N}$$ The negative sign means it acts downward.
Step 12Check moments: every force on the free body passes through point $A$, so each moment arm is zero and $\sum M_{A}=0$ is satisfied automatically; it gives no new equation, which is why a particle has only force equations.
Step 13Compute the magnitude: $$F=\sqrt{F_x^2+F_y^2}=\sqrt{(338.8)^2+(294.9)^2}\ \mathrm{N}=449\ \mathrm{N}$$
Step 14State the direction: $$\theta=\tan^{-1}\!\left(\frac{294.9}{338.8}\right)=41.0^{\circ}$$ below the negative $x$ axis, so $\mathbf{F}$ pulls down and to the left.
Step 15Check reasonableness: the three known forces have a net pull up and to the right, so the holding force must point down and to the left, and $449\ \mathrm{N}$ is comparable in size to the given forces.
Worked Solution
Free-body diagram of ring A
**Given:** $F_1=600\ \mathrm{N}$ at $20^{\circ}$, $F_2=450\ \mathrm{N}$ at $60^{\circ}$ above $-x$, $F_3=300\ \mathrm{N}$ down. **Find:** $F$. Let $\mathbf{F}=F_x\mathbf{i}+F_y\mathbf{j}$. $$\rightarrow^{+}\ \sum F_x=600\cos20^{\circ}-450\cos60^{\circ}+F_x=0\ \Rightarrow\ F_x=-(563.8-225.0)=-338.8\ \mathrm{N}$$ $$\uparrow^{+}\ \sum F_y=600\sin20^{\circ}+450\sin60^{\circ}-300+F_y=0\ \Rightarrow\ F_y=-(205.2+389.7-300)=-294.9\ \mathrm{N}$$ $$F=\sqrt{338.8^2+294.9^2}=449\ \mathrm{N},$$ directed down and to the left at $\tan^{-1}\!\left(\dfrac{294.9}{338.8}\right)=41.0^{\circ}$ below the negative $x$ axis.
Problem 15
Ch. 3 · Q15 — Towing bridle with unequal cable angles
A tug tows a barge through a bridle. The towing pendant pulls on connecting ring $A$ with a force of $5.00\ \mathrm{kN}$ along the positive $x$ axis (the tow line). Two bridle cables run back from $A$ to the barge: cable $AB$ makes $25^{\circ}$ with the tow line on one side, and cable $AC$ makes $40^{\circ}$ with the tow line on the other side. All forces lie in the horizontal plane.
Plan view of a towing bridle at ring A
Determine the tension in bridle cable $AB$.
Solution
3.55 kN
Free-body diagram
Free-body diagram of ring A
Step 1Draw the free-body diagram: isolate ring $A$ in plan view. Three forces act: the pendant force of $5.00\ \mathrm{kN}$ along $+x$, $T_{AB}$ pulling back toward $B$ at $25^{\circ}$ above the negative $x$ axis, and $T_{AC}$ pulling back toward $C$ at $40^{\circ}$ below the negative $x$ axis.
Step 2List knowns and unknowns: known tow force $5.00\ \mathrm{kN}$, angles $25^{\circ}$ and $40^{\circ}$; unknown $T_{AB}$ and $T_{AC}$.
Step 3State the model: ring $A$ is a particle moving at constant velocity (equilibrium) under coplanar forces in the horizontal plane; the weight of the ring and cables is neglected.
Step 4Set axes: $+x$ along the tow line (forward) and $+y$ toward the $B$ side.
Step 5Resolve $T_{AB}$ into components: $-T_{AB}\cos25^{\circ}$ in x and $+T_{AB}\sin25^{\circ}$ in y.
Step 6Resolve $T_{AC}$ into components: $-T_{AC}\cos40^{\circ}$ in x and $-T_{AC}\sin40^{\circ}$ in y.
Step 7Sum forces in y: $$\uparrow^{+}\ \sum F_y=T_{AB}\sin25^{\circ}-T_{AC}\sin40^{\circ}=0$$
Step 8Sum forces in x: $$\rightarrow^{+}\ \sum F_x=5.00\ \mathrm{kN}-T_{AB}\cos25^{\circ}-T_{AC}\cos40^{\circ}=0$$
Step 9Check moments: every force on the free body passes through point $A$, so each moment arm is zero and $\sum M_{A}=0$ is satisfied automatically; it gives no new equation, which is why a particle has only force equations.
Step 10Rearrange the y-equation: $$T_{AC}=T_{AB}\frac{\sin25^{\circ}}{\sin40^{\circ}}=0.6575\,T_{AB}$$
Step 11Substitute into the x-equation: $$T_{AB}\cos25^{\circ}+0.6575\,T_{AB}\cos40^{\circ}=5.00\ \mathrm{kN}$$
Step 12Collect terms: $$T_{AB}(0.9063+0.5037)=1.4100\,T_{AB}=5.00\ \mathrm{kN}$$
Step 13Solve for $T_{AB}$: $$T_{AB}=\frac{5.00\ \mathrm{kN}}{1.4100}=3.55\ \mathrm{kN}$$
Step 14Check reasonableness: $T_{AC}=0.6575(3.546)=2.33\ \mathrm{kN}$. The cable more nearly in line with the tow ($AB$ at $25^{\circ}$) carries the larger share, and the forward components $3.21+1.79=5.00\ \mathrm{kN}$ balance the tow force.
Worked Solution
Free-body diagram of ring A
**Given:** tow force $5.00\ \mathrm{kN}$ along $+x$; cable $AB$ at $25^{\circ}$ and cable $AC$ at $40^{\circ}$ from the tow line. **Find:** $T_{AB}$. **FBD at $A$:** $$\uparrow^{+}\ \sum F_y=T_{AB}\sin25^{\circ}-T_{AC}\sin40^{\circ}=0$$ $$\rightarrow^{+}\ \sum F_x=5.00-T_{AB}\cos25^{\circ}-T_{AC}\cos40^{\circ}=0$$ From the y-equation $T_{AC}=T_{AB}\dfrac{\sin25^{\circ}}{\sin40^{\circ}}=0.6575T_{AB}$. Then $T_{AB}\left[0.9063+0.6575(0.7660)\right]=1.4100\,T_{AB}=5.00\ \mathrm{kN}$, so $$T_{AB}=3.55\ \mathrm{kN},\qquad T_{AC}=0.6575(3.546)=2.33\ \mathrm{kN}.$$
